As of Oct '17, I believe they have been in business for a year. I'm hopeful that they will be able to project and plan better to avoid being under stocked. 

I've been twice, and will keep going!  I'm very glad to have discovered them. They're on the top floor / roof deck of Antioch University.

Based on a dine-out experience of pastries and specialty coffees:

Perhaps my low-star rating is due to the overwhelming "hype" that surrounds Alessia Pâtisserie. Truthfully, I had high hopes I would love Alessia's pastries given that the owner is a former Renaud's employee and there seems to be a lot of inspiration drawn from the classic French bakery we all love. 

My latte was perfect and the coffee seemed to have great flavor. To my surprise, when I opened up the boxes I discovered something totally unexpected! These pastries look nothing like what I was expecting. They were intricately designed and creative. In fact, I give props to the artistry that went into creating some thing beautiful and unique. 

Unfortunately the pastries I received for my birthday breakfast simply were not good. They certainly did not live up to the reputation. The one that looks like a little mouse was dry and cakey. The pumpkin pastry had some red stuff inside, too many baking spices, pumpkin flavoring and tasted confectionery. 

Overall lacked precision and focus- other than being pretty and too sweet- they were not at all memorable.

In the end I think the bakery is trying to do too much. Rather than focus on mastering the simple and classic pastries, I see reinventions and "upgrades" on things that maybe were better off plain and simple. I do hope to go into the restaurant at some point to update my review on the experience and ambience found at the brick and mortar site. 

As far as presentation goes, I give an A for effort! They are cool and artsy. That being said, some of the other dishes I see posted look to me like they are just too experimental or overdone. When I see the term "pâtisserie" I expect classic French pastries- I think Alessia's bakery is cute, but it's not a French Pâtisserie and is still figuring out its own identity-hopefully they'll find it! For now, This would be a place I would go for a brunch with my mom to be "cutsie"but not necessarily for my every day breakfast or go to bakery.

Amazing, never disappoints. Coffee is fresh and delicious - same goes for their food. Adorable little patio that is dog friendly and they share the inside with a wine bar. Great spot to meet friends, go on a breakfast/lunch date, or get some work done!

The coffee was good, but they need to work out some communication and logistic kinks they're experiencing. I was charged twice (the iPad cash register is a cool idea when it works), and the communication between the two owners wasn't great.

Came here for breakfast.  Service is fast, and the food is awesome, but I seem to keep ordering the same generic egg dish.  The place is big and every time I've been, we always seem to get seated immediately.
Dinner was so good came back for breakfast the country fried steak was a steak hash browns and biscuit all homemade and excellent.  Don't miss a chance to eat here. Been open almost 90 years

The first place I went to when I got to SB to satisfy my 6am coffee cravings. A lovely little coffee joint that actually had a few people coming in at that time. Their coffee is superb and they have a yelp check in that's nice to use :)

Wow. Amazing space. Very solid complex but balanced beers, with good variety in regular menu and creative limited releases. Pumpkin Spice on nitro is what a pumpkin beer should taste like. IPA with grapefruit was citrusy without overwhelming. Food and wine tasting in same space but you cant carry beer between the spaces. One of the better breweries in SoCal, easily the best I've visited in Santa Barbara area. Will eagerly return.

Where do I begin. If I had the option of giving this Denny's zero stars, I would. We drove three hours to meet my dad for breakfast and we were starving. The waitress came and took our drink orders, brought our drinks and we ordered our food. After forty five minutes of waiting, we finally asked the waitress what was going on with our order. She replied that it was the next one up. Well she came back with half our order and apologized that somehow our ticket was lost and she had to take our order again. My burger was so sloppy it didn't even have cheese. She then said it would be about five minutes more. Well five minutes turned into twenty and by the time ny daughterband sisters food came everyone else was done.The manager came to our table and asked if something was wrong with our food. Like are you serious. He said our food was free, but in the end only took 20% off. He also had the audacity to ask my dad if he was going to tip them. Save yourself from this place and go to McDonald's. Manager doesnt know how to run this place.
Perfect little breakfast place.  Very simplistic, but flavorful!  Totally going back.
I've had a lot of fish tacos in my life, but I swear these ones are THE best. The best. I live in the Bay Area now after several years here, and I would drive down just to eat these tacos.

Ridiculously expensive. Like absurdly expensive.  
But great service. There were 3 guys behind the counter. All very friendly and helpful.  They eagerly gave suggestions and talked the food up. But you could tell they were being genuine about it not and not just telling you what you wanted to hear. 
I only ordered a cookie. It was good. Not 4 dollars good though.  The food looks good but i don't know if I will ever be willing to shell out to much money for what it is offering.
Located in the Public Market. Great iced mocha latte with coconut milk. Staff was very friendly. Quick service. Highly recommend for coffee.

Like I was transported right to Paris on a busy Saturday morning at the patisserie... the pastries were as delicious as they were stunning, coffee was amazing, and the mushroom toast is out of this world! I will be back regularly!

By far the best breakfast I've had in a restaurant. I found this restaurant because I was actully looking for a place to piss. After I was done, I walked out and saw the amazing looking pancakes. Then I told myself, oh heck, why not. So I stayed for breakfast. 

I usually don't eat sweets for breakfast, but the pancake is the best ever, especially the blueberry ones. ummm...makes me want to go there now. 

Of all the times I've been to Santa Barbara, this is one of my must go to places to get my day started. Then its off to Solvang to get drunk.

This review isn't about the food, because due to the AWFUL service we never got to even try their food. We walk in and no one is at the hostess stand. Meanwhile multiple servers walk by us and ignore us. Finally after standing around 10 minutes someone finally acknowledged us. They wrote our name and said they were clearing a table and we can sit. Well , no one cleared the table and they all moved with zero urgency. Finally after waiting an additional 10 minutes, we left and went next door where we were served right away and had great food.

A likable place with a fantastic selection of teas and coffees.  The staff is always friendly, knowledgeable and helpful.  The coffees I've sampled have always been a step above Starbucks.  The pastries, which come from other sources, aren't always the best, but they're adequate.  

The seating area is rather small but there is a communal table where it's easy to meet people in the mornings.  A positive crowd comes in here then.  

I wish they had wifi.  I suppose they have their reasons, but I'd be here a lot more if they did.

Overall I likable relaxed shop.

Coffee and food are good. The large lced latte in the giant glass is fun and delicious. Their bagels are good. The toast with avocado and tomato is very good.  The service is not so good. I have to repeat my order at least twice everytime and the poorly trained staff still get it wrong over and over again.

I really enjoyed our little Sunday brunch that we had here.  Lot of families around later on in the morning, but it added a nice atmosphere.  The decor inside can make the place seem a bit moody, but the terrace is quaint and the servers were efficient and professional.  Also, this place is located in a cute little alleyway that perfectly showcases the slow, artistic side of Santa Barbara.  

I ordered the French toast with strawberries and port wine reduction.  
Drool.

There's no way to describe Joe's other than to say that it's a good, solid restaurant serving staple dishes done well. This place isn't serving truffle aioli or burgers topped with gruyere on brioche buns or a little speck of fancy sprouts on a big, bare white plate... it's just a real restaurant. How often can you even say that anymore? It reminds me of home in Missouri.

The portions are absolutely massive, and I'd say anything on the menu is a safe bet. They start you with fresh sourdough, crackers, butter on a plate and salsa. The fried chicken with mashed potatoes and vegetables is killer. The club sandwich, fish and chips and fried chicken sandwich all seemed to be 100% home made. No frozen fries here. No skimping on portions. No nonsense. 

This is also a place with a full bar where you can get white wine or pink martinis or bottles of beer. Whatever you want. Your server might just be the guy wearing a bow tie in the black and white picture hanging on the wall. Everything from the red-and-white checkered tablecloths to the hanging white lights charms the crap out of you. On the way to the restroom you'll see fresh pies. 

So, if you want to get a taste of what old school quality must have been like in 1928 when they opened, go to Joe's. Minus one star for the 1920s acoustics... if you're next to a table of kids it's loud loud loud.

Good food, great customer service, stopped by for breakfast, when I was passing through, my only complaint was I thought it was more of a healthy foods restaurant, I had a breakfast omelette with potatoes, tasty but not particularly healthy. I still give it 3 stars.

This place is adorable and the cupcakes are great! The staff were incredibly friendly and seemed to really enjoy working there. I got the strawberry blush cupcake and it had a wonderful, real strawberry flavor to it. My husband loved his pumpkin cheesecake cupcake too. So much so, that he wolfed it down before I got to have a taste! I highly recommend this place.

This place was excellent. I had the granola, berries and yogurt, and my husband had the breakfast sandwich. I think it's the best granola I've ever had. The cakes and baked goods look amazing, and I will be going back tomorrow for more. Why can't I have a place like this by my house?

Coffees good I love the Mexican and Cinnamon Bun coffee 
And pastries are really good as well my favorite would be a warm cinnamon bun? I'm not sure if that's what it's called but it's a croissant cinnamon roll with raisins 
A bit pricy just for coffee but if your in a rush and don't have a car to go to Starbucks this place is worth it lol

Beer was good but the service was terrible. Three servers on hand and only six customers and absolutely no friendliness or connection. We weren't told anything about the beers, weren't asked if we liked it, no eye contact - just flat out rude. I felt like I was bothering them by even asking them for a beer. This coming from a local who finally came by to support a truly local brewery - I will not return nor recommend this to friends and visitors. Sell your product! Have some passion! Tell us stories about your beer - that is what sets you apart.

That's what I'm talking about. We stopped in because my husband and I have now become coffee snobs. We wanted to pick up some whole beans before heading back home to San Diego. We bought a bag of one of the medium roast coffee (Brazil) and also the light roast Ethiopian to drink on our way back for the drive. The "light" roast is actually flavorful and strong, like I like it! The staff was really friendly and told us a little about the different roasts. There is plentiful seating inside and out, and there is a 15 mins parking spots out front for those wanting to go in for a quick drink. 

There are also some goodies you can grab (muffins, cookies, etc) if you need a quick snack. The coffee shop is about a block from State Street and the Paseo Nuevo shops.

Glorious.  Flavorful, plentiful, and they're quite generous with samples in case you're having trouble making up your mind.

I get the peach gelato in a cone, and it's a perfect accompaniment to a walk along State Street.  Get extra napkins, though, because it can get a little drippy.  

There's one loading zone space in front of the store, so if you're lucky you can send a friend in while you wait.

Great selection of coffees.  Really quaint and comfortable environment.  It is supposed to be quirky so if you are looking for a pristine facility, get over it.  The roasts lean on the dark and very robust side, which suits me well.  Staff were friendly and helpful.

Absolutely wonderful! You order at the window, and they bring your food to the table. They have about 7 tables inside where the water and condiments are, and 10 or so very nice covered picnic tables with benches outside. It's quaint, but roomy. 

I ordered the YOLO: if you want to really splurge and you like biscuits and gravy, this is the dish for you! I've never had a fried chicken breast with my B&G, and I feel like I've been living life all wrong. It is SO TASTY. The chicken breast was juicy, crispy, seasoned well; the gravy was out of this world...but the piece de resistance was the biscuit. I haven't had a biscuit homemade from real lard/butter (whatever they use), in a long time. It was fluffy and dense all at once. It didn't stick to the roof of my mouth like a cheap bread would, nor did it soak up everything completely. Their biscuit is the base for many of their dishes, and I can understand why; they are very very good.

I came here via groupon. Best deal ever! Worth the trip! Happy eating!

I went down to Paseo Nuevo's 805 Boba to get a cold drink this weekend and stumbled upon this cute display of Collective Kitchen fresh baked goods! I decided to get the marshmallow chocolate chip cookie  AMAZING! I don't know how they make the marshmallow melted into the cookie so perfectly but it was a combo of a chocolate chip cookie/s'mores deal... just amazing!  I got a coffee drink to go with it and it was a perfect combo!

Mmmmm.  I am making my jOe face.  

The breakfast burrito says "tri-tip" and I was expecting something close to carne asada but it was more like tender pot roast, and it was bomb.

The service was great and the ambiance was a cool combinatioin of modern and rustic.  It was mustic.

My brother-in-law says it was his favorite place to drink when he lived here.  He says the drinks are so strong that'd he have to return and ask for more soda or juice.  You know the drinks are strong when your vodka & cranberry looks like a 7-up.

Recommended.

Me and my friends came to Santa Barbara for a day trip and was told this was an excellent place to go for afternoon coffee and pastries. And it definitely is! Very small but comforting and intimate, we had 2 passion fruit macaroons, chocolate eclair, and a croissant with jam plus 2 coffee's and a hot chocolate. The lady behind the counter was super nice and inviting, I'm not sure if she was the owner or not, but either way I loved her! Definitely will come back whenever we plan another trip to Santa Barbara.
